claim: People rarely notice a useful source analog unaided (about 30% solve vs about 75% after a hint); the bottleneck is retrieval/noticing, not applying.
agent_test: Compare O7 with the source cued by the scaffold vs left for the model to recall unaided, equal tokens, on problems with a known structural analog.

claim: Comparing two analogs and writing the shared principle raises transfer over one analog (45% vs 21% unprompted, 80% vs 53% total); written schema quality predicts transfer (91% of good-schema writers solved unprompted). The schema link is correlational, and a student power note suggests the effect is small.
agent_test: One analog vs two analogs plus a required written common rule, then solve; score on held-out structural-twin problems.

claim: Retrieval of an analog depends on both surface and structural similarity; with neither shared, spontaneous use falls to about 13% (69% with both).
agent_test: Retrieve sources from a memory store by relational description vs by keyword or embedding; compare hit rate at fixed budget.

claim: Trying the target problem first (even failing), then seeing the analog, raises spontaneous transfer (over 80% vs about 5% baseline) compared with studying for recall.
agent_test: Order test: attempt first then read the case, vs read case first; same tokens.

claim: LLM success on letter-string analogies does not generalise to altered alphabets: GPT models fall (mean 0.35-0.49 vs humans 0.753) while humans stay flat; 2024 frontier models fall further with each domain shift (GPT-4o 0.85/0.63/0.48 Latin/Greek/Symbol; adults 0.88/0.91/0.89).
agent_test: After any analogical mapping, rerun it on a surface-changed twin and require the same answer.

claim: Part of the letter-string failure is exact counting and position tracking, not analogy: GPT-4 with code execution matched humans on counterfactual tasks (P=0.496), while plain GPT-4 was below humans. Source is the original authors' reply only. Published PNAS Nexus version: humans vs GPT-4+code P=0.92; GPT-4+CoT still below humans (P=3e-8); the code model forbidden to run code scored 22.5% vs 21.7% for GPT-4, so code caused the gain; GPT-4 found the letter interval only 10.8% of the time. Still one research group and GPT-4 only.
agent_test: Run counterfactual letter-string tasks with and without a code tool; verify the gap closes at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs do near narrative analogies fairly well but far ones below chance (models 39.6% vs humans 94.1%); surface-similar distractors drive failure (33.9% when a far analogy competes with a near distractor). Independent benchmarks agree on surface pull: in StoryAnalogy models chose hard negatives 56-60% of the time vs 29-37% for the true analogy; AnaloBench 4-way accuracy falls from 89.1 to 60.7 (GPT-4, 1 to 30 sentences) and is near random for most models at 30 sentences.
agent_test: Plant surface-similar distractor sources in the memory store; measure whether the agent picks the structural match.

claim: Having the model state the abstract message or principle before matching lifts far-analogy accuracy (up to 30 points) but can hurt near analogies; knowledge-first then examples gave the best Codeforces result.
agent_test: Principle-first vs direct matching, split by near and far cases.

claim: Re-expressing a problem in structured, decomposed form lifts the same model by large margins (RAVEN: OPT-1.3B from 20-30% to over 70%; GPT-3 up to 92.6% on a sub-task; Mind's Eye +27.9 points zero-shot via simulator). Hand-built encodings, so it measures representation, not automatic re-description.
agent_test: Ablate the restatement step on ARC-like and matrix items at equal tokens; compare model-written vs hand-written restatement.

claim: Self-generated analogical prompting gives small gains on maths and code (GSM8K 75.0 to 77.8; MATH 33.0 to 37.3 for GPT-3.5; Codeforces Acc@1 8 to 15%), and needs a strong model; small models do better with retrieved examples. At equal sample or token budget (Liu 2025, 6 models, maths and MMLU) analogous prompting falls behind plain CoT: limit accuracy 81.3 vs 88.2 (Qwen2.5-7B), 77.0 vs 83.1 (GLM-4-9B), 68.2 vs 71.3 (LLaMA-3-8B).
agent_test: Self-generated vs retrieved vs none, by model strength, at equal tokens.

claim: The gain from self-generated analogs may come from example correctness, not relevance: random biology examples did about 2.5% better than relevant self-generated math ones; example accuracy 62% (relevant) vs 72% (none) vs 86% (random same-type). Contradicts the cognitive reading of K10.
agent_test: Compare relevant vs irrelevant vs code-verified-correct recalled cases.

claim: Plain prompting mode-collapses on idea diversity; an analogy-first pipeline raises domain diversity 100-115% and solution diversity 90-173% (Vendi) and novelty rates (Claude 1.6% to 50.4%). Novelty was LLM-judged with a human pairwise check (AR picked as more novel 78% of pairs, kappa .445). Preprint. Caution: an execution study (Si 2025) found LLM ideas lost their novelty edge after 100-hour implementation.
agent_test: Generate N candidates with plain vs analogy-first, measure Vendi and a retrieval-based novelty check, then validity by code.

claim: LLM ideas are rated more novel but slightly less feasible than expert ideas, with low diversity (about 5% non-duplicate seeds) and weak self-judgement (best 71.4%). Execution check (Si 2025, N=43 projects): AI idea scores fell 1.0 to 2.0 points after execution vs about 0 to 0.6 for human ideas (FDR p 0.001-0.025); ideation and execution scores barely correlate.
agent_test: Overgenerate, dedupe, judge with an outside check rather than the generator.

claim: Current LLMs are argued to reach combinational and exploratory but not transformational creativity (Boden); this is conceptual, with no direct empirical test.
agent_test: Build tasks that need a rule change in the space and test whether a rule-change operator succeeds where plain sampling fails.

claim: In human and GPT-3 creativity tests originality and usefulness trade off (r about -.56 to -.61); GPT-3 more useful, humans more original.
agent_test: Select candidates on both originality and a code-testable usefulness check; compare to selecting on originality alone.

claim: Embedding similarity is a poor analogy finder at higher abstraction levels, and models are pulled by distractor words and surface content. Further: relation-aware retrieval with gold sub-concepts reached only 24.5% Hit@1 vs 19.5% embedding-only (Barakat 2026); GPT-4 and Llama-405B drop 0.4-0.8 under semantic distractors where humans drop little (Musker 2025).
agent_test: Strip surface content before mapping vs not; compare.

claim: GPT-3 on Webb's 2023 tests matched humans on matrices (OR 1.88 generative, 6.27 multiple choice, N=40), letter strings and SAT-style analogies but was weaker on far story analogies; training contamination could not be excluded and K05 shows brittleness.
agent_test: Use only novel, unpublished items.

claim: Mapping quality can be checked by code: one-to-one, argument-consistent, scored by shared higher-order relational structure (SME); multi-constraint scoring (structure, meaning, goal) is the competing ACME view, not opened.
agent_test: Typed mapping check in code vs model self-assessment of mapping quality.

claim: Running a simulation and trusting its output beats model-only reasoning on physics-like tasks (Mind's Eye 46.0 points few-shot; 1.3B plus simulator matches 175B).
agent_test: Offer a code sandbox for simulating the analog's causal model vs none.

claim: Thought Propagation (solve analogous easier problems then revise) gives +12 to +15 points on its own benchmarks; authors only, abstract only for one record.
agent_test: One-layer analog-and-revise vs direct, with outside check of the analog answer.

claim: Retrieving a relevant analog from a large store by model reading alone is close to chance: AnaloBench top-10 of 200 stories was near random for GPT-4 Turbo and Claude 2 except at 1 sentence. Relation-aware descriptions raise retrieval (average 0.557 to 0.673 with sub-concepts) but top-1 hit stays 17.5 to 24.5%.
agent_test: Index analogs by typed relational descriptions and test Hit@1 and Hit@5 against name-only and embedding retrieval at fixed store size.

claim: At equal compute, simple chain of thought with majority voting beats complicated prompting strategies, including analogous prompting, on maths and science QA with 4B-9B models; compute-matched evidence for O7 on non-maths tasks is still absent.
agent_test: Run O7 vs best-of-N CoT at equal tokens on structure-bound tasks (altered alphabets, ARN far items), not GSM8K.

claim: Counting and indexing, not analogy, drive most letter-string failures: code access closes the gap on counterfactual alphabets while chain of thought does not. No 2025-26 reasoning-model test was found.
agent_test: Compare a reasoning model with and without a code tool on altered alphabets; log whether it chooses code.

claim: Different example or analog contexts per sample may beat the same context repeated at equal sample count (varied-context agents beat self-consistency in 5 of 6 model-task pairs, Gemini 1.0). Old models; weak evidence.
agent_test: Give each of N samples a different analog and compare with N samples sharing one analog.
